title: Securing Cloud-Native Financial Microservices
business: A regional fintech firm managing high-frequency transaction microservices deployed on Kubernetes.
problem: The development team frequently commits hardcoded API credentials and misconfigured container manifests to the internal registry, leading to potential unauthorized access and compliance violations.
solution: Trivy provides a unified scanner that integrates into the CI/CD pipeline to perform static analysis on container images and Infrastructure-as-Code files, identifying vulnerabilities, secret leaks, and misconfigurations before deployment.
steps: Integrate Trivy as a binary step within the CI pipeline runner.
Configure Trivy to scan the local filesystem for IaC files like Kubernetes manifests.
Define a severity threshold to fail builds containing High or Critical findings.
Output results in JSON format for ingestion by the security dashboard.
outcome: The organization achieves a consistent security baseline where insecure configurations and exposed secrets are blocked automatically, reducing the manual audit burden on the security team.
limitation: Trivy performs static analysis, meaning it cannot detect runtime-only vulnerabilities or misconfigurations that emerge only after environmental variables are injected at execution time; verify this by comparing static scan results against runtime security monitoring logs.
